There is no worker or waiter count. Process memory bounds how many operations run and wait.

## If a limit is reached

| Limit reached | Result |
| --- | --- |
| A file over its slot or `FILE_MAX_MIB`, or a request over `FILES_MAX_MIB` | `WYRD_VERIFICATION_413_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` before anything runs |
| The server's verification staging is full (`scribe.outbox_capacity` or `scribe.outbox_bytes`) | Direct and new queued calls: `WYRD_VERIFICATION_429_STAGING_FULL` with `Retry-After`, before anything is staged. Accepted queued executions stay queued until there is room for their result |
| `TIMEOUT_MS` in `verify` | `WYRD_VERIFICATION_504_EXECUTION_TIMED_OUT` |
| No direct execution slot, or process memory or scratch cannot hold a Python operation's waiting bytes, frees too late for its envelope, or cannot hold a workspace | `verify`: `WYRD_SERVER_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| No queued execution slot, or process memory or scratch cannot hold the same | Queued: stays queued, attempt not counted |
| Every model call in use | The call waits for one, within the execution's deadline |
| Verification disabled on this process | `WYRD_SERVER_503_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` |
| A publication over `FILE_MAX_MIB`, `FILES_MAX_MIB`, or `PUBLICATIONS_MAX` | The publish call is refused with the limit and nothing is published; the execution's accepted publications and their totals survive retries and recovery |
| `AGENT_TOOL_MAX_CALLS` | The step fails or the check is `inconclusive`, with `WYRD_VERIFICATION_422_TOOL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` in its `reason`; a program cannot catch it |
| Any other limit in a step or check, including `AGENT_CODE_BUDGET_MS` | The step fails or the check is `inconclusive`, with the limit in its `reason` |

# MCP tools

Page: /wyrd/reference/mcp-tools/

> Wyrd MCP tool names, permissions, shapes, and query limits.

The server serves MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28 over HTTP at `/mcp`; `wyrd mcp proxy` relays the same tools over stdio.

## Discovery

- `tools/list` returns each tool's current input and output JSON Schemas; named shapes below, such as `VerificationRequest`, are those schemas. Unknown argument fields are refused.
- Read tools and `wyrd.guide` are always listed. Write, revoke, reset, and delete tools are listed only to callers holding their permission. Listing grants nothing.
- Credentials and secrets are never returned.

## Agent frameworks

Tool names contain dots, which many model providers refuse, so each framework forwards an alias.

| Framework | Tested configuration |
| --- | --- |
| OpenAI Agents SDK (Python) | `mcp_config={"convert_schemas_to_strict": True, "include_server_in_tool_names": True}`; aliases such as `mcp_wyrd__wyrd_guide` |
| Pydantic AI | `MCPToolset(url, headers=...).renamed({"wyrd_guide": "wyrd.guide", ...})`, one entry per tool |
| Google ADK | `ADK_ENABLE_MCP_MODERN_PROTOCOL=1` and `GOOGLE_API_USE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE=false`; override `McpToolset.get_tools` to return copies whose `name` is the alias |

## Investigation guide

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `wyrd.guide` | Any caller | `{topic}` → `{topic, steps, examples}` | Static workflow guidance |

`topic` is `start`, `overview`, `cards`, `verification`, or `bifrost_sql`; `start` is the entry point for a new agent. Each example has `tool`, `purpose`, and `arguments`; angle-bracket placeholders stand for discovered values.

## Cards and verification

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cards.list` | `cards:read` | List filters and optional cursor → `{items, next_cursor}` | List Card summaries |
| `cards.get` | `cards:read` | `{card_ref}` or `{kind, card_uid}` → `{card, created_at, updated_at}` | Read one Card; pass exactly one form |
| `verification.get_binding` | `cards:read` | `{binding_id}` → binding status | Read one binding |
| `verification.get_execution` | `verifier:read` on the execution's Verifier | `{execution_id}` → execution status with its compact result | Read one execution |
| `verification.get_execution_details` | `verifier:read` on the execution's Verifier | `{execution_id}` → execution details: checks, provenance, steps, and pinned evidence | Read what one completed execution ran |
| `verification.list_invocations` | `verifier:read` on the execution's Verifier | `{execution_id, limit?, cursor?}` → `{execution_id, status, items, next_cursor, history}` | Page invocation attempts and their progress |
| `verification.list_publications` | `verifier:read` on the execution's Verifier | `{execution_id, limit?, cursor?}` → `{execution_id, items, next_cursor}` | Page publication names, kinds, and producers |
| `verification.get_publication` | `verifier:read` on the execution's Verifier | `{execution_id, step_id, name, attempt, item_index?, iteration_index?}` → publication | Read one publication's JSON value or manifest |
| `verification.download_publication` | `verifier:read` on the execution's Verifier | The `verification.get_publication` arguments plus `path` for a directory → `{plan, size_bytes, sha256}` | Plan one publication file's download |
| `verification.evidence` | `verifier:run` | `{files: [{sha256, size_bytes}]}` → `{uploads: [{sha256, upload_id, plan}]}` | Plan uploads for files the tenant lacks; complete each with `POST /v1/cards/upload/{upload_id}/complete` |
| `verification.publish_evidence` | `verifier:run` on each subscribed Verifier | `{repository: "owner/name", tags: {commit}, input, value}` → `{evidence_id, repository, tags, input, status, matched_subscriptions, recorded_at}` | Publish a deferred input for one commit; waiting executions resume; `status` is `accepted` or `replayed` |
| `verification.execute` | `verifier:run` on exact Verifier | Verifier, subject, optional `run_id`, and named input declarations → `VerificationResult` | Verify now and store the result; no Operator dispatch |
| `verification.enqueue` | `verifier:run` on exact Verifier | The `verification.execute` arguments plus optional `idempotency_key` → `{execution_id}` | Queue a verification; poll `verification.get_execution` |
| `verification.cancel` | `verifier:run` on the execution's Verifier | `{execution_id}` → `{execution_id, status}` | Cancel unfinished queued work; settled work keeps its status |
| `verification.decide_approval` | `verifier:approve` on the execution's Verifier and `cards:read` on its subject | `{execution_id, approval_id, decision, reason?}` → `{approval_id, status, actor_id, decided_at, reason}` | Approve or reject one pending approval; the same execution continues; the same decision and reason replays |

`cards.list.filter` is a query string, such as `labels.env = "prod" and labels.deprecated not exists`, over `labels.<key>`, `annotations.<key>`, and `attributes.<key>`, with `=`, `in`, `not exists`, `and`, `or`, and `not`; at most 64 predicates. A caller passes `next_cursor` back unchanged with the same filters. Missing and foreign-tenant Cards look the same. `verification.execute` refuses a scheduled drift Verifier.

## Bifrost

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bifrost.list_tables` | `bifrost_table:read` | `{}` → `{tables}` | List readable tables |
| `bifrost.describe_table` | `bifrost_table:read` | `{namespace, name}` → table description | Read one table's schema and layout |
| `bifrost.query` | scoped `bifrost_query:read` | `{sql, deadline_ms?, max_rows?, max_bytes?}` → `{columns, rows, terminal}` | Run one bounded `SELECT` |
| `bifrost.validate_predicate` | scoped `bifrost_query:read` | `{namespace, name, expression}` → `{expression}` | Check one `WHERE` filter over a table's columns, up to 8 KiB, and return it normalized |

Gateway request and response payload columns also need `gateway_payload:read`.

### Query limits

| Bound | Default | Maximum |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SQL text | Required | 65,536 UTF-8 bytes |
| `max_rows` | 1,000 | 10,000 |
| `max_bytes` | 4 MiB | 16 MiB |
| `deadline_ms` | Server policy | 4,294,967,295 ms; minimum 1 |

`sql` is one DataFusion SQL `SELECT` with fully qualified table names. Rows are positional arrays in `columns` order. A result is complete only when `terminal.outcome` is `"success"`; a result over `max_rows` or `max_bytes` is refused, never truncated.

## Principal credentials

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `principals.list_credentials` | `service_accounts:write` | `{principal_id}` → CredentialListResponse | List credentials, including expired and revoked |
| `principals.revoke_credential` | `service_accounts:write` | `{principal_id, credential_id}` → CredentialRevoked | Stop token issuance from a credential |
| `principals.set_workload_restriction` | `*` | `{principal_id, workload_restriction}` → PrincipalSummary | Replace a Service account's workload restriction; a family makes it that family's unique scheduled runtime account |

A token already minted from a revoked credential lapses within five minutes.

## Operator connections

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `operator_connections.list` | `operators:read` | `{}` → `{connections}` | List connections |
| `operator_connections.get` | `operators:read` | `{connection_id}` → OperatorConnectionView | Read one connection |
| `operator_connections.create` | `operators:write` | `{request: CreateOperatorConnectionRequest}` → OperatorConnectionView | Create a Slack, PagerDuty, or HTTP connection |
| `operator_connections.update` | `operators:write` | `{connection_id, request}` → OperatorConnectionView | Patch a connection; provider and name are fixed |
| `operator_connections.disable` | `operators:write` | `{connection_id}` → OperatorConnectionView | Disable a connection |

## GitHub connection

The read is listed for every caller; the writes are listed only for a caller
holding `identity_connections:write`. GitHub's setup and OAuth callback are
browser redirects, not tools.

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `github_connection.get` | `identity_connections:write` | `{}` → GithubConnectionView | Read the tenant's redacted connection |
| `github_connection.connect` | `identity_connections:write` | `{}` → GithubConnectResponse | Begin a connection; a signed-in human opens the returned install URL |
| `github_connection.disconnect` | `identity_connections:write` | `{}` → GithubConnectionView | Fence GitHub work and release the installation |

## Gateway administration

Gateway tools address resources by exact `name` and never call a model.

| Tool | Permission | Input → output | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `gateway.list_provider_credentials` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → `{items}` of credential views | List credentials |
| `gateway.list_provider_deployments` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → `{items}` of deployments | List deployments |
| `gateway.get_provider_credential` | `gateway:read` | `{name}` → credential view | Read one credential |
| `gateway.get_provider_deployment` | `gateway:read` | `{name}` → deployment | Read one deployment |
| `gateway.get_fallback_policy` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → fallback policy | Read the fallback policy |
| `gateway.get_governance_policy` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → governance policy | Read limits, budgets, and pricing |
| `gateway.get_capture_policy` | `gateway:read` | `{}` → versioned capture policy | Read the capture policy |
| `gateway.put_provider_credential` | `gateway:write` | ProviderCredentialWrite → credential view | Create or rotate a credential |
| `gateway.put_provider_deployment` | `gateway:write` | ProviderDeployment → deployment | Create or replace a deployment |
| `gateway.apply_provider_deployments` | `gateway:write` | ProviderDeploymentsApply → applied credentials and deployments | Write credentials and deployments in one transaction |
| `gateway.put_fallback_policy` | `gateway:write` | FallbackPolicy → fallback policy | Replace the fallback policy |
| `gateway.put_governance_policy` | `gateway:write` | GovernancePolicy → governance policy | Replace the governance policy |
| `gateway.put_capture_policy` | `gateway:write` | CapturePolicyWrite → versioned capture policy | Replace the capture policy |
| `gateway.revoke_provider_credential` | `gateway:write` | `{name}` → credential view | Revoke permanently |
| `gateway.delete_provider_credential` | `gateway:delete` | `{name}` → `{}` | Delete an unreferenced credential; absent succeeds |
| `gateway.delete_provider_deployment` | `gateway:delete` | `{name}` → `{}` | Delete a deployment; absent succeeds |
| `gateway.delete_fallback_policy` | `gateway:write` | `{}` → `{}` | Restore the default |
| `gateway.delete_governance_policy` | `gateway:write` | `{}` → `{}` | Restore the default |

A managed secret is write-only. A credential still referenced by a deployment cannot be deleted.

## Errors

A refusal is a JSON-RPC error or an `isError` result carrying a Wyrd problem with `code` and remediation.

| Code | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `WYRD_QUERY_400_INVALID_SYNTAX` | Malformed `cards.list` filter |
| `WYRD_VALA_413_QUERY_RESULT_TOO_LARGE` | The query result is too large to return |

# Stored-secret encryption

Page: /wyrd/reference/stored-secret-encryption/

> The [kms] server settings that select the wrapping backend and keys for stored secrets, with provider setup, startup refusals, and runtime errors.

`wyrd-server` encrypts every recoverable secret it stores with a fresh 256-bit data key, and wraps that key with the deployment wrapping key that `[kms]` selects. Settings are read once at startup from the `[kms]` table of the [server TOML file](/wyrd/reference/verification-runtime-limits/#server-toml-file). Environment variables override them, and a change takes effect after a restart.

## Settings

| Setting | Environment variable | Applies to | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | `WYRD_KMS_BACKEND` | all | `file`, `memory`, `gcp_kms`, `aws_kms`, or `vault_transit`. Required |
| `active_key` | `WYRD_KMS_ACTIVE_KEY` | all | The key that wraps new data keys. Required |
| `retained_keys` | `WYRD_KMS_RETAINED_KEYS` | all except `memory` | Keys still allowed to unwrap existing values. A comma-separated list in the variable |
| `key_dir` | `WYRD_KMS_KEY_DIR` | `file` | Directory holding one key file per key name. Required for `file` |
| `endpoint` | `WYRD_KMS_ENDPOINT` | `gcp_kms`, `aws_kms`, `vault_transit` | API base URL. Required for `vault_transit`; GCP defaults to `https://cloudkms.googleapis.com`, AWS to the key ARN's regional endpoint |
| `vault_mount` | `WYRD_KMS_VAULT_MOUNT` | `vault_transit` | Transit mount path. Default `transit` |
| `vault_namespace` | `WYRD_KMS_VAULT_NAMESPACE` | `vault_transit` | Vault Enterprise namespace |
| `vault_token_file` | `WYRD_KMS_VAULT_TOKEN_FILE` | `vault_transit` | Owner-only file holding the Vault token, re-read on every call |
| — | `WYRD_KMS_VAULT_TOKEN` | `vault_transit` | The Vault token itself; environment only |

An environment variable that is set but empty, or not UTF-8, refuses startup.

## Key references

| Backend | `active_key` and `retained_keys` |
| --- | --- |
| `file`, `memory`, `vault_transit` | A key name: 1 to 128 ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-`, or `.`, not starting with `.` |
| `gcp_kms` | A CryptoKey resource name without a version: `projects/<p>/locations/<l>/keyRings/<r>/cryptoKeys/<k>` |
| `aws_kms` | A key ARN in `aws`, `aws-cn`, or `aws-us-gov`: `arn:<partition>:kms:<region>:<account>:key/<id>`. Aliases are refused |

Each stored value records the key that wrapped it. Opening a value whose key is neither active nor retained refuses without calling the backend.

## Backends

| Backend | Wrapping key | Authentication | Wrap context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | A file in `key_dir` named after the key, mode `0600`, holding 32 random bytes as base64 | File ownership | AES-256-GCM associated data |
| `memory` | 32 random bytes generated at startup and lost on exit; values stored under it cannot be opened after a restart | None | AES-256-GCM associated data |
| `gcp_kms` | A symmetric `ENCRYPT_DECRYPT` CryptoKey; Cloud KMS selects the primary version to encrypt and the needed version to decrypt | The Google identity GCS storage uses: `GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_JSON_BASE64` (base64 service-account JSON), else `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON` (service-account JSON), else application default credentials: `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS`, the gcloud default, or the metadata server | `additionalAuthenticatedData` |
| `aws_kms` | A symmetric key; AWS selects its key material on decrypt | The standard AWS credential chain: environment, web identity, container, or instance metadata | Encryption context `wyrd-context` |
| `vault_transit` | A Transit key of an AEAD type such as `aes256-gcm96`; Transit keeps old versions for decrypt | The Vault token | `associated_data` |

Provider credentials are refreshed before they expire. One wrap or unwrap call to a remote backend is bounded to 10 seconds and follows no redirects.

The workload needs these provider permissions on every active and retained key:

| Backend | Permission |
| --- | --- |
| `gcp_kms` | `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt` and `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` (role `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`) |
| `aws_kms` | `kms:Encrypt` and `kms:Decrypt` |
| `vault_transit` | `update` on `<mount>/encrypt/<key>` and `<mount>/decrypt/<key>` |

## Provider setup

Wyrd neither creates nor deletes wrapping keys. Provision each key before the server starts, and grant the server's workload only the permissions above.

### `file`

```bash
mkdir kms
openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n' > kms/v1
chmod 0600 kms/v1
```

Set `key_dir` to the `kms` directory and `active_key` to `v1`. The user running the server must own the file.

### `vault_transit`

```bash
vault secrets enable transit
vault write -f transit/keys/wyrd-secrets type=aes256-gcm96
vault policy write wyrd-kms - <<'HCL'
path "transit/encrypt/wyrd-secrets" { capabilities = ["update"] }
path "transit/decrypt/wyrd-secrets" { capabilities = ["update"] }
HCL
vault token create -policy=wyrd-kms -field=token > vault-token
chmod 0600 vault-token
```

Set `endpoint` to the Vault address, `active_key` to `wyrd-secrets`, and `vault_token_file` to the token file. A Vault Agent may renew or replace the token in that file. Rotate with `vault write -f transit/keys/wyrd-secrets/rotate`; existing values stay readable and `active_key` does not change.

### `gcp_kms`

```bash
gcloud kms keyrings create wyrd --location=us-central1
gcloud kms keys create wyrd-secrets --keyring=wyrd --location=us-central1 --purpose=encryption
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding wyrd-secrets --keyring=wyrd --location=us-central1 \
  --member=serviceAccount:<server-service-account> --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
```

Set `active_key` to `projects/<project>/locations/us-central1/keyRings/wyrd/cryptoKeys/wyrd-secrets`. Run the server as that service account, point `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` at its key file, or set its key JSON in `GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_JSON_BASE64` (base64-encoded) or `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON`.

GCS storage and Cloud KMS read the same variables, so a server that already reaches its bucket through one of them uses that service account for Cloud KMS too. Grant it the key role above; storage permissions do not include Cloud KMS. When both inline variables are set, `GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_JSON_BASE64` wins, and a value in it that is not valid base64 of UTF-8 selects no inline key rather than falling back to `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON`.

### `aws_kms`

```bash
aws kms create-key --key-spec SYMMETRIC_DEFAULT --key-usage ENCRYPT_DECRYPT --query KeyMetadata.Arn --output text
```

Allow `kms:Encrypt` and `kms:Decrypt` on the printed ARN to the server's IAM role, through the key policy or an IAM policy, and set `active_key` to that ARN.

## Example

```toml
[kms]
backend = "aws_kms"
active_key = "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/2222bbbb-2222-2222-2222-222222222222"
retained_keys = ["arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/1111aaaa-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"]
```

## Renew, replace, or revoke a stored secret

Each resource that stores a secret offers three separate actions under its existing name or id and permission:

- **Renew encryption** reseals the unchanged secret under a fresh data key wrapped by the active key. The resource's identity, settings, and state, and the secret the provider accepts, do not change, so clients need no reconfiguration. A human connection keeps its revision and its sessions. Only modification metadata changes: `updated_at`, and an Operator connection's `updated_by`.
- **Replace** stores a new secret supplied by the administrator, without opening the old one. Wyrd never mints one.
- **Revoke** stops Wyrd using the secret. It does not revoke the credential at its provider; do that at the provider, then replace or revoke it in Wyrd.

| Resource | Renew encryption | Replace | Revoke |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Operator connection | `POST /v1/operator-connections/{connection_id}/renew-encryption`, `wyrd operator-connection renew-encryption` | Update with a new credential | Disable |
| Gateway managed secret | `POST /v1/admin/gateway/provider-credentials/{name}/renew-encryption`, `wyrd gateway credential renew-encryption` | Put the credential again | Revoke |
| Human OIDC connection | `POST /v1/identity/oidc/connections/{id}/renew-encryption` | Stage, test, and activate a candidate | Delete the connection |
| Trusted issuer | `POST /v1/admin/trusted-issuers/renew-encryption?issuer=`, `wyrd auth trusted-issuer renew-encryption` | `PUT /v1/admin/trusted-issuers/client-secret?issuer=` with `{"client_secret": "..."}`, `wyrd auth trusted-issuer replace-secret`; workload bindings are kept | Delete the issuer |
| Platform OIDC connection | `POST /platform/oidc/connection/renew-encryption` | `PUT /platform/oidc/connection` | `DELETE /platform/oidc/connection` |

`wyrd auth trusted-issuer replace-secret` reads the new secret from `--client-secret-file` or `WYRD_ISSUER_CLIENT_SECRET`, never from an argument.

A renewal or trusted-issuer replacement reads the secret, seals outside any database transaction, and stores the result only if the resource still holds the secret it read. One that races a replacement, revocation, or deletion loses with a `409` and the other change stands; neither restores a revoked or deleted resource.

| Resource | `404` | `409` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Operator connection | No such connection in the caller's tenant | The connection changed between the read and the store. A disabled connection renews and stays disabled |
| Gateway managed secret | No such credential | The credential is revoked, holds no managed secret, or changed |
| Human OIDC connection | No Active or Candidate connection with the id; an inactive connection is not found | The connection holds no client secret, or was deactivated, replaced, or renewed after the read |
| Trusted issuer | No such issuer in the caller's tenant | The issuer holds no client secret, or was deleted or changed |
| Platform OIDC connection | No connection is configured | The connection holds no client secret, or was removed or replaced |

Every action answers `503` with the stored secret unchanged when the key service or the store is unavailable. A trusted-issuer replacement with an empty secret answers `400`.

## Rotate or recover the wrapping key

Changing `active_key` affects only new writes. Existing values keep the key that wrapped them, and stay readable while that key is listed in `retained_keys`. A platform administrator moves them with one maintenance pass at a time:

```bash
WYRD_PLATFORM_CREDENTIAL=... wyrd platform stored-secrets maintain --mode routine --server https://wyrd.example.com
```

```text
mode: routine
current: 0
changed: 9
remaining: 0
bounded: false
```

| Mode | Effect on each value not under `active_key` | Use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `routine` | Rewraps its data key under `active_key`. The data key and payload ciphertext are kept | Planned rotation |
| `recovery` | Reseals the value under a fresh data key wrapped by `active_key` | A wrapping key or data key may be exposed |

Native provider rotation (`gcloud kms keys versions create`, `vault write -f transit/keys/<key>/rotate`, AWS automatic rotation) keeps the same reference: values stay readable and need no pass.

**Planned rotation**

1. Provision the new key and grant the server its permissions.
2. Restart every server with the new key as `active_key` and the old key in `retained_keys`.
3. Run `--mode routine` until `remaining` is `0` and `bounded` is `false`.
4. Remove the old key from `retained_keys` only when no backup you may restore holds values under it, then restart.

**Compromise recovery**

1. Contain the incident: revoke the exposed access and stop any server that should no longer run.
2. Provision a fresh key never used as `active_key` before, including by an earlier routine pass.
3. Restart every server with the fresh key active and the old keys retained. Stop every process still writing under an old key.
4. Run `--mode recovery` until `remaining` is `0` and `bounded` is `false`. Never run `--mode routine` into this key; nothing stops an administrator from choosing the wrong mode.
5. Replace each exposed credential at its provider and in Wyrd. Resealing does not revoke a credential an attacker already copied.

If containment removed access to an old key, recovery cannot open the values under it. Restore controlled read access to that key, or replace each credential through its owner without opening it. Removing a key from `[kms]` and restarting refuses every value under it until the key is listed again; Wyrd has no action that disables a key or cancels work already admitted.

### Maintenance pass

`POST /platform/stored-secrets/maintenance` with a platform session; the CLI command above calls it. It needs the platform `platform_credentials:write` permission; a tenant token is refused. The destination is always `active_key`; the request cannot name a key, tenant, or resource.

| Request field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `mode` | `routine` or `recovery`. Required |
| `limit` | Most values the pass attempts to move, at least 1. Omitted, the pass attempts all within half the server's request timeout. CLI `--limit` |

| Report field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `current` | Values the pass saw already under `active_key` |
| `changed` | Values the pass moved |
| `remaining` | Values the pass read that are still not under `active_key`: failed, changed concurrently, or left by the bound |
| `bounded` | The pass stopped at `limit` or its time budget; stores it did not read are not counted |
| `failures` | Up to 100 values the pass could not move, each with `store`, `data_tenant_id` (absent for the platform connection), `owner`, and `reason` |

Counts describe only what one pass saw. `remaining: 0` does not prove that no backup, cache, or still-running old server depends on a key. Repeat with the same mode while `remaining` is above `0` or `bounded` is `true`; a repeated pass leaves values it already moved unchanged.

| `reason` | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `key_not_allowed` | The value's key is neither active nor retained |
| `key_unavailable` | The backend refused or could not serve the call. Vault Transit also answers a value copied from another owner this way |
| `unopenable` | The value is not a Wyrd envelope or did not authenticate under its owner |
| `invalid_owner` | The row's owner metadata cannot bind a value |
| `concurrent_change` | The owner replaced or renewed the value first; that change stands |

The pass answers `503` with `reason: kms_not_configured` when the server has no `[kms]`, and `401` without a platform session.

## Startup refusals

Startup fails and names the first offending setting; the message never contains a key, token, path, or URL.

| Condition | Setting named |
| --- | --- |
| `backend` missing or not a listed value | `backend` |
| `memory` on a production server | `backend` |
| `active_key` missing or malformed for the backend | `active_key` |
| A retained key malformed, equal to `active_key`, or listed twice | `retained_keys` |
| `retained_keys` with `memory` | `retained_keys` |
| A setting that does not apply to the selected backend | that setting |
| `key_dir` missing for `file`, or a key file missing, readable by others, or not 32 bytes of base64 | `key_dir` |
| `endpoint` not an `http` or `https` URL, `http` on a production server, or missing for `vault_transit` | `endpoint` |
| Not exactly one of `vault_token_file` and `WYRD_KMS_VAULT_TOKEN` for `vault_transit` | `vault_token` |
| GCP or AWS credentials cannot be loaded | `backend` |

Wyrd never generates a substitute key when a configured one is missing.

## Errors

Errors at runtime, when a stored secret is written or opened:

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| The stored bytes are not a Wyrd envelope | Unknown format |
| Encrypting the value failed | Encryption failed |
| The value's key is neither active nor retained | Key not allowed; the backend is not called |
| The value, its wrapped data key, or its expected owner was changed | Authentication failure; Vault Transit answers a changed wrap context as `refused` |
| The unwrapped data key is not 32 bytes | Invalid data key |
| The backend refuses, times out, cannot be reached, or has no usable credential | Backend unavailable, with the backend and one of `refused`, `timeout`, `transport`, or `credential` |

# Error codes

Page: /wyrd/api/errors/

> Every stable Wyrd error code with its HTTP status, title, and fix.

Every Wyrd error carries a stable `code`, such as `WYRD_SPEC_400_VALIDATION`: the area, the HTTP status, and the cause. Branch on `code`, never on the message. The same code reaches you over HTTP, MCP, the CLI, and every SDK.

Over HTTP an error is an RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` body:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | The stable code from the tables below |
| `status` | The HTTP status |
| `title` | A fixed summary of the code |
| `detail` | What went wrong in this request |
| `remediation` | What to do about it |
| `details` | Fields specific to the error, such as `rule` and `path` for a validation failure |

This page is generated from the error definitions in the Wyrd source.

## WYRD_AGENT

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_PROMPT_CARD` | 404 | Prompt Card not found | Load or register the referenced Prompt Card in the local prompt registry before resolving the agent. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_RUNTIME_LOCAL_TOOL_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Runtime-local tool not found | Register the named tool in the local Skald tool registry before loading the Agent Card. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_TOOL` | 404 | Tool not registered for agent | Register the tool before running the agent or remove the tool call from the provider response. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_404_TOOL_NOT_IN_AGENT` | 404 | Tool not attached to agent | Attach the runtime-local tool to this agent or adjust the model response. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_409_PROVIDER_MISMATCH` | 409 | Provider mismatch | Run the agent with a prompt targeting the same provider as the agent's resolved prompt. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_412_DELEGATION_DEPTH` | 412 | Agent delegation depth exceeded | Reduce nested agent-as-tool calls or restructure the workflow so the delegation chain stays within the cap. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_CALLBACK_RETURN_TYPE` | 422 | Callback returned wrong type | Return None to continue, return a replacement value of the expected type, or raise an exception to abort the run. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_INVALID_ARGUMENT` | 422 | Invalid argument | Correct the argument value; see details for the expected type or constraint. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_LOOP_MESSAGE_TYPE` | 422 | Loop message type mismatch | Re-render the conversation message against the active provider; loop messages must match the provider's message schema (OpenAi / Anthropic / Gemini / Custom). |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_MISSING_NAME` | 422 | AgentCard name is missing | Set a card name before saving or projecting the agent to a card envelope. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_MISSING_VERSION` | 422 | AgentCard version is missing | Set a concrete semantic version before saving or projecting the agent to a card envelope. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_PROMPT` | 422 | Agent prompt rendering failed | Inspect the prompt template and the variables passed to the agent run. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_RUNTIME_LOCAL_TOOLS_NOT_REGISTRABLE` | 422 | Runtime-local tools are not registrable | Remove runtime-local tool names before registration; local save, load, and run remain available. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_STRUCTURED_INVALID` | 422 | Structured response invalid | The model refused, or did not correct its answer within the Agent's iteration budget; simplify the response schema, clarify the Prompt, choose a model that follows structured output, or raise max_iterations. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_TOOL_ARGS` | 422 | Tool arguments invalid | Adjust the provider-emitted tool arguments to match the tool input schema. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_422_VALIDATION` | 422 | AgentCard validation failed | Fix the Agent Card envelope, metadata, prompt reference, tools, or run_config fields. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_499_CALLBACK_ABORTED` | 499 | Callback aborted run | Inspect the callback exception and either return None to continue or return a valid replacement value. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_500_CALLBACK_PANIC` | 500 | User-supplied callback panicked | Inspect the panic payload and fix the callback implementation; callbacks must not panic. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_500_JOURNAL` | 500 | Journal append failed | Inspect the journal backend; for the no-op journal this should never fire. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_500_MAX_ITERATIONS` | 500 | Agent exceeded max iterations | Raise the run's max_iterations or adjust the agent prompt and tools so the loop can terminate. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_502_PROVIDER` | 502 | Provider call failed | Inspect the provider backend and retry once it is healthy. |
| `WYRD_AGENT_504_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Agent run exceeded configured timeout | Increase the run timeout or reduce iteration count and tool latency. |

## WYRD_AUTH

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_BAD_TOKEN_FORMAT` | 400 | Access token header malformed | Use `X-Wyrd-Access-Token: Bearer &lt;token&gt;` with a single Bearer credential. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` | 400 | Delegation chain exceeds maximum depth | Reduce the delegation chain; the caller's existing `act` chain plus the requested hop must be at most 5 layers. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_DEVICE_AUTHORIZATION` | 400 | Device authorization did not issue a credential | Keep polling on `authorization_pending`, poll five seconds slower on `slow_down`, and start a new login on any other `details.error`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_HUMAN_CONNECTION_REQUIRED` | 400 | Human login uses the tenant OIDC connection | Trusted issuers and `[[trusted_issuers]]` accept only `principal_kind = workload`. Configure human sign-in through the tenant OIDC connection API: PUT /v1/identity/oidc/candidate, POST /v1/identity/oidc/candidate/test, then POST /v1/identity/oidc/candidate/activate. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_INVALID_CARD_REF_VERSION` | 400 | Non-human principal CardRef.version must be an exact Pin | Re-issue the request with `card_ref.version` set to an exact `Pin`, for example `1.2.3`; version requirements are rejected for card-bound principals. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_INVALID_NONCE` | 400 | Invalid OIDC nonce | Restart the login flow. The ID token nonce must match the server-stored login nonce. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_INVALID_STATE` | 400 | Invalid OIDC state | Restart the login flow. The callback state is single-use and must match the server-stored login state. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_PRINCIPAL_KIND_CARD_KIND_MISMATCH` | 400 | CardRef cannot be bound to a non-human principal | Only Service and Agent cards bind to non-human principals. Re-issue the request with a `card_ref` referencing a Service or Agent card. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_SIGNED_WORKLOAD_MISMATCH` | 400 | Workload context differs from the signed root | The bearer token already pins a workload root, which a request header cannot change. Send the same `x-wyrd-workload-uid` or none, or obtain a separate token for the other release. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_UNSUPPORTED_CLIENT_AUTH` | 400 | Unsupported OIDC client authentication | Use `SecretBasic` or `SecretPost` with a client secret, or `Public` without one. `private_key_jwt` is not supported for tenant connections. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_400_UNSUPPORTED_GRANT_TYPE` | 400 | Unsupported grant_type | Use one of the supported grants listed in `details.supported_grant_types`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_API_KEY_INVALID` | 401 | API key not found, revoked, or hash mismatch | Issue a new credential with `wyrd principal credential issue --principal &lt;id&gt;` and update the deployment secret. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_CREDENTIAL_REVOKED` | 401 | Credential revoked | The credential was explicitly revoked. Re-authenticate or request a new credential. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_DELEGATION_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` | 401 | Delegation chain in token exceeds maximum depth | The presented JWT's `act` chain exceeds the verifier's maximum delegation depth. Re-issue from a shorter chain. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_INVALID_CARD_REF` | 401 | Non-User token card_ref claim absent or malformed | Re-issue the token via `POST /auth/token`; ensure the bound non-human principal has a valid structured card_ref. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_INVALID_TOKEN` | 401 | Invalid token | Re-authenticate to obtain a valid token signed by the current issuer key. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_ONE_TIME_CODE_INVALID` | 401 | One-time code not accepted | Ask a tenant administrator for a new invitation or reset code; each code is single-use and expires. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_PASSWORD_INVALID` | 401 | Username or password not accepted | Check the tenant, username and password and try again; a forgotten password is reset with a code from a tenant administrator. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_REFRESH_REUSED` | 401 | Refresh token reused | Re-authenticate. The refresh token family has been revoked because a rotated token was reused. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_REFRESH_REVOKED` | 401 | Refresh token revoked | Re-authenticate to obtain a new refresh token. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_TOKEN_EXPIRED` | 401 | Token expired | Re-authenticate to obtain a fresh token. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Not authenticated | Present a valid Wyrd token as `X-Wyrd-Access-Token: Bearer &lt;token&gt;`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_401_WORKLOAD_UID_REFUSED` | 401 | Workload root refused | `workload_uid` is optional. When supplied it must name an active, registered Service Card version in this tenant that the account's workload restriction allows; unknown and foreign roots are refused identically. Omit it to authenticate the account without workload context, or register the release and pass its exact Card UID. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_ORIGIN_REFUSED` | 403 | Request origin refused | Send browser-session requests from the Wyrd application's own origin; cross-site and origin-less browser-session mutations are refused. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_PRINCIPAL_ORPHANED` | 403 | The backing Service or Agent card has been soft-deleted | Re-declare the card or use a different principal to obtain a token. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_RECENT_LOGIN_REQUIRED` | 403 | Recent sign-in required | Sign in again with your password or SSO, then create the key within five minutes; an API key or recovery session cannot create one. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_UNREPRESENTABLE_DELEGATION` | 403 | Delegated permissions cannot be represented | The subject's and actor's shared permissions cannot be represented by token scopes, so the exchange issued no token. Exchange with grants whose exact shared authority fits the supported scopes, such as both parties holding the same explicit gateway deployment or model grant. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_403_WORKLOAD_CONTEXT_REQUIRED` | 403 | Workload context required | This account is restricted to one workload family, so Card-attributed emission needs the exact release root. Exchange the key with `workload_uid`, send `x-wyrd-workload-uid`, or use the WyrdState loaded for that release. Generic authorized calls do not need a root. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_404_ADMIN_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Admin resource not found in tenant | Confirm the issuer URL (and subject for bindings) and that the resource exists in the current tenant. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_404_PRINCIPAL_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Requested principal not found in tenant | The principal named by the `subject_token` or `actor_token` no longer exists in the current tenant. Re-authenticate both parties and retry the exchange. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_ADMIN_CONFLICT` | 409 | Admin resource already exists or is still referenced | A trusted issuer or workload binding with this key already exists, or the issuer still has live bindings. Use a distinct key, or delete the bindings first (or with --cascade). |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_CONNECTION_CONFLICT` | 409 | Tenant OIDC connection conflict | Re-read GET /v1/identity/oidc/connections and retry with the current `expected_revision`. Activation also requires a valid recovery API key for a headless principal of this tenant that holds `identity_connections:write`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_CONNECTION_NOT_TESTED` | 409 | Tenant OIDC candidate is not freshly tested | Run POST /v1/identity/oidc/candidate/test against this exact candidate revision, complete the provider sign-in at the returned authorization_url, and activate within 15 minutes of that successful test. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_409_WORKLOAD_BINDING_CONFLICT` | 409 | Workload family already has a runtime account | Each Service family has at most one family-restricted runtime account. Issue another credential on that account for rotation or concurrent releases, or first set the existing account's restriction to `unrestricted`. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_413_CARD_SCOPE_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Card scope too large | Reduce or split the selected root's declared Card graph so its transitive observation-target scope fits the token size limit, or select a root with a smaller graph. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_429_PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS` | 429 | Too many password attempts | Wait `details.retry_after_seconds` until the fixed attempt window ends, then try again. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_503_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | OIDC discovery unavailable | Retry with backoff. Do not re-authenticate; this is an infrastructure or issuer-discovery failure. |
| `WYRD_AUTH_503_VERIFY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Auth verify backend unavailable | Retry with backoff. Do not re-authenticate; this is an infrastructure failure, not a credential failure. |

## WYRD_CFG

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_CFG_400_INVALID_TOML` | 400 | wyrd.toml failed TOML syntax parse | Check the TOML syntax in your wyrd.toml file, or the file path if the read itself failed. |
| `WYRD_CFG_400_NAME_DEFAULT_REJECTED` | 400 | wyrd.toml cannot default `name` | Remove the `name` key from [defaults] or [kind.&lt;X&gt;]. Every card must author its own name. |
| `WYRD_CFG_400_SCHEMA_MISMATCH` | 400 | wyrd.toml schema mismatch | Compare the file against the documented wyrd.toml schema in architecture/wyrd-design.md. |

## WYRD_CLIENT

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_400_CONFIG_INVALID` | 400 | Client configuration is invalid | Correct the client configuration field named in details and rebuild the client. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_401_NO_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | No client credentials available | Set WYRD_ACCESS_TOKEN, WYRD_WORKLOAD_TOKEN with WYRD_TENANT, or WYRD_API_KEY, pass an explicit client credential, or add a default api_key to the Wyrd credentials file. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_401_SAVED_LOGIN_UNUSABLE` | 401 | Saved user login cannot be used | Run `wyrd auth login --server &lt;url&gt; --tenant &lt;tenant&gt;` again, select the intended tenant with the client tenant option or WYRD_TENANT, or pass an explicit credential. The details reason names the failure. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_413_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Sealed batch exceeds the client message ceiling | Reduce the row or batch size, or raise max_message_bytes within the server's accepted ceiling. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_422_ROW_DESERIALIZATION` | 422 | Query row deserialization failed | Align the caller's row type with the columns and types the query selects. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_429_QUEUE_FULL` | 429 | Client ingestion queue is saturated | No row of the refused record was admitted: flush or back off, then resubmit the same record. Sustained refusals mean the producer outpaces delivery; every refusal bumps the drop counter. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_503_TRANSPORT_DOWN` | 503 | Client transport is unavailable | Verify the endpoint, DNS, TLS material, and network reachability, then retry once the transport recovers. |
| `WYRD_CLIENT_504_FLUSH_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Client flush exceeded its drain deadline | Increase flush_timeout_ms or reduce the in-flight batch size so the drain can complete. |

| `WYRD_CLI_400_MCP_HOST_SELECTION` | 400 | MCP host selection required | Pass --host for each host to connect (codex, claude-code, copilot-cli, vscode, cursor, pi, hermes); install and open the host first if none is detected. |
| `WYRD_CLI_400_QUERY_CONFIG` | 400 | Query configuration missing | Pass --server or set WYRD_SERVER_URL; the credential comes from the ambient chain. |
| `WYRD_CLI_400_SERVER_HOST_UNSUPPORTED` | 400 | Server host unsupported | Run the server on macOS on aarch64 or Linux (glibc) on x86_64 or aarch64, or use the official container image. |
| `WYRD_CLI_400_USAGE` | 400 | Invalid command usage | Correct the arguments; run the command with --help for its accepted arguments. |
| `WYRD_CLI_401_NO_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | No Wyrd credentials | Set WYRD_ACCESS_TOKEN, configure workload identity or WYRD_API_KEY, or add [default].api_key to ~/.config/wyrd/credentials.toml. |
| `WYRD_CLI_401_NO_PLATFORM_CREDENTIAL` | 401 | No platform credential | Set WYRD_PLATFORM_CREDENTIAL to a platform credential for this deployment. |
| `WYRD_CLI_401_NO_REFRESH_TOKEN` | 401 | No refresh token | Set WYRD_REFRESH_TOKEN to the refresh token to rotate. |
| `WYRD_CLI_409_MCP_HOST_INSTALL` | 409 | MCP host installation failed | Fix the problem reported for each failed host, then rerun; hosts reported as added, updated, or unchanged are already connected. |
| `WYRD_CLI_409_SERVER_INSTALL_INCOMPLETE` | 409 | Server installation incomplete | Remove the named version directory, then rerun `wyrd server install`; nothing was activated. |
| `WYRD_CLI_409_SERVER_VERSION_INCOMPATIBLE` | 409 | Server version incompatible | Upgrade the wyrd CLI to the server's version line (uv add --upgrade wyrd-ai, or pnpm add wyrd-ai@latest), then retry. |
| `WYRD_CLI_422_SERVER_RELEASE_UNVERIFIED` | 422 | Server release unverified | Retry the install; if it fails again, report the release. The current installation is unchanged. |
| `WYRD_CLI_500_IO` | 500 | CLI filesystem IO failed | Check file paths and permissions, then retry. |
| `WYRD_CLI_500_OUTPUT` | 500 | CLI output failed | Retry the command or use --format text. |
| `WYRD_CLI_500_QUERY` | 500 | Oracle query failed | Inspect the stable query error and terminal diagnostics, then retry. |
| `WYRD_CLI_503_CLIENT_TRANSPORT` | 503 | Wyrd server unavailable | Check the server URL and network connectivity, then retry. |
| `WYRD_CLI_503_MCP_PROXY` | 503 | MCP proxy failed | Check that the Wyrd server URL is reachable and serves /mcp, and that the host launches `wyrd mcp proxy` over stdio, then reconnect the host. |
| `WYRD_CLI_503_SERVER_DEV` | 503 | Local server setup failed | Follow the stage's recovery guidance and rerun with the same tenant and configuration directory; active tenant credentials are never reissued. |
| `WYRD_CLI_503_SERVER_RELEASE_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Server release unavailable | Check network access to github.com, then retry; the current installation is unchanged. |

## WYRD_GATEWAY

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_400_INVALID_CONFIGURATION` | 400 | Invalid gateway configuration | Correct the field named in `details.field`. Path and body names must match, credential bindings and secret backends must be configured on the server, and deployments must reference an active credential for the same provider. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_400_INVALID_REQUEST` | 400 | Invalid gateway request | Correct the field named in `details.field`. Models use the `&lt;provider&gt;/&lt;model&gt;` projection and a fallback override is a non-empty, duplicate-free list that excludes the requested model. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_404_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE` | 404 | Gateway model unavailable | Request a model the tenant has deployed for this operation, or ask a tenant administrator to add a deployment or fallback candidate. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_404_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Gateway resource not found in tenant | List provider credentials or deployments to confirm the name exists in the current tenant. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_409_RESOURCE_CONFLICT` | 409 | Gateway resource conflicts with its current state | A revoked credential cannot be replaced, a credential referenced by a deployment cannot be deleted, a pricing version's content is immutable, and an identical batch creation still pending cannot be repeated. Use a new name or version, remove the referencing deployment first, or vary the batch metadata. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_422_COST_UNBOUNDED` | 422 | Gateway call cost cannot be bounded | A budget applies or unknown cost is rejected, so the call needs active pricing for its model and a bounded request such as a maximum output token count. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_429_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Gateway budget exceeded | Wait for the next budget period, request a smaller bounded call, or ask a tenant administrator to raise the budget. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_429_CAPTURE_STAGING_FULL` | 429 | Gateway capture staging is full | Nothing of the refused call was charged or sent upstream: retry the identical call after `details.retry_after_seconds`, or lower the request rate. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_429_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Gateway limit exceeded | Retry after `details.retry_after_seconds`, reduce concurrency, or ask a tenant administrator to raise the limit. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_502_UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` | 502 | Gateway upstream unavailable | Retry with backoff. If failures persist, a tenant administrator should check the deployment's provider, credential, and fallback configuration. |
| `WYRD_GATEWAY_504_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | 504 | Gateway deadline exceeded | Retry with a longer deadline or a smaller request. |

| `WYRD_REGISTRY_409_REPOSITORY_SELECTION_CONFLICT` | 409 | Repository selection changed during declaration | Another declaration selected details.selected first; its Cards stay registered. Read the Repository Card, then declare again to select your policy over it. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_409_SPEC_DRIFT` | 409 | Re-declare with the same identity but a different spec_hash; same-version cards are immutable | Bump `metadata.version` to publish a new spec, or revert your spec to match the declared version. |

| `WYRD_REGISTRY_500_VERSION_CONFLICT` | 500 | Card uid mismatch for same identity | Internal invariant violation; report with the request id and audit_id. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_503_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE` | 503 | Transient Postgres or RLS misconfiguration; retry with backoff | Retry with exponential backoff (60s cap). If persistent, check Postgres connectivity, the tenant row, and the RLS role bindings. |
| `WYRD_REGISTRY_507_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED` | 507 | Artifact verification failed | Re-upload the artifact and retry finalization. |

| `WYRD_SDK_400_RUNTIME_HYDRATION_FAILED` | 400 | Runtime Card hydration failed | Provide the required custom interface/load arguments or regenerate a complete compatible bundle. |
| `WYRD_SDK_400_UNHYDRATED_ARTIFACT` | 400 | Card bundle is missing artifact payloads | Run wyrd pull for the intended root Card with --output-dir &lt;dir&gt; and without --metadata-only, then load that directory. |
| `WYRD_SDK_404_UNKNOWN_ALIAS` | 404 | Unknown WyrdState alias | Use an alias returned by the loaded WyrdState bundle. |
| `WYRD_SDK_404_UNKNOWN_VERIFIER` | 404 | Verifier is not bound to this subject | Name a Verifier bound in `verified_by` to the view's subject Card, or open the view on the Card that binds it. |
| `WYRD_SDK_409_BIFROST_ALREADY_STARTED` | 409 | WyrdState Bifrost writer is already started | Reuse the state's existing writer, or shut it down and create a new WyrdState to start again. |
| `WYRD_SDK_409_BIFROST_CLOSED` | 409 | WyrdState Bifrost writer is closed | Create a new WyrdState and start its Bifrost writer; a shut-down state stays closed to writes. |
| `WYRD_SDK_409_STATE_CONFIG_FROZEN` | 409 | WyrdState configuration is already fixed | Call configure once, before startup and before opening a Run, or construct another WyrdState for a different configuration. |
| `WYRD_SDK_409_TELEMETRY_PROVIDER_EXISTS` | 409 | An OpenTelemetry provider is already installed | Turn off Wyrd's managed telemetry setup and add each state's Wyrd span, log, and metric exporters to the application's own providers. |
| `WYRD_SDK_409_VERIFICATION_CANCELLED` | 409 | Verification execution was cancelled | Read the execution's accepted evidence, or submit the verification again; a cancelled execution never resumes. |
| `WYRD_SDK_422_VERIFICATION_DATA_INVALID` | 422 | Verification data does not match the requested type | Match the requested type to the check's declared data schema, use a union or decoder for mixed shapes, or read the result without a type. |
| `WYRD_SDK_503_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_FAILED` | 503 | Telemetry flush failed | Check the OpenTelemetry exporter's logs and the state's credentials, then retry flush or shutdown. |
| `WYRD_SDK_504_TELEMETRY_FLUSH_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Telemetry flush timed out | Check that the Wyrd server's OTLP endpoint is reachable, raise the OpenTelemetry SDK export timeout if spans are large, and retry flush or shutdown. |
| `WYRD_SDK_504_VERIFICATION_WAIT_TIMEOUT` | 504 | Verification execution did not settle in time | Wait again with the same execution ID, or read its status; a submission lost before queue acceptance never settles and must be submitted again. |

| Code | Status | Title | Fix |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_400_INPUT_INVALID` | 400 | Invalid verification input | Send `{ verifier_card_uid, card_uid, inputs }` where inputs maps each declared Verifier slot to a json, file, artifact, or trace value; run_id and execution_route_overrides are optional. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_400_INVALID_TARGET` | 400 | Invalid verification run target | Target an existing binding, or an active Verifier Card UID plus an active subject Card UID in this tenant, whose implementation accepts the requested input. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_400_INVALID_WINDOW` | 400 | Invalid Drift window | Send a UTC half-open drift_window with start before end spanning at most 31 days. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_APPROVAL_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification approval not found | Read the execution and decide an approval_id listed in its approvals. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_BINDING_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification binding not found | Read the owner Card's card.status.verification.binding_ids and retry with one of those binding IDs. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_EXECUTION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification execution not found | Use the execution_id returned by POST /v1/verification/enqueue in the same tenant; a just-accepted execution may take a moment to become visible. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_PUBLICATION_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification publication not found | List GET /v1/verification/executions/`{execution_id}`/publications and select a listed name with its exact producer attempt, item_index, and iteration_index. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_404_TARGET_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Verification target not found | Use an active Verifier Card UID and an active subject Card UID declared in the caller's tenant. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_APPROVAL_NOT_PENDING` | 409 | Verification approval not pending | An accepted decision is final and an ended execution takes none: read the execution for the occurrence's status, and decide a pending occurrence of a current execution instead. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_BASELINE_LEGACY` | 409 | Verification baseline legacy | Register a new Verifier version so its baseline is refitted under the current format. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_BASELINE_NOT_READY` | 409 | Verification baseline not ready | Poll the Verifier Card's card.status.verification.baseline until it is ready, then retry. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT` | 409 | Verification evidence conflict | Accepted evidence is never replaced: republish the original content to replay its receipt, or publish the new content for a new commit. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_EVIDENCE_UNMATCHED` | 409 | Verification evidence unmatched | Check the input name and repository: publish only an input a Verifier bound to the connected repository declares with deferred: true. Nothing was retained, so publish again once a binding subscribes. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_SNAPSHOT_INCOMPLETE` | 409 | Verification snapshot incomplete | Check Bifrost publication for the named source executions, then submit a new turn to the group. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_409_VERIFIER_NOT_READY` | 409 | Verifier not ready | Poll the Verifier Card's card.status.verification.baseline until it is ready, then retry. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_413_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` | 413 | Verification input too large | Keep the request body and each evidence file within the Deployment's verification limits, or upload large files through verification.evidence and pass them by digest. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_421_WRONG_TARGET` | 421 | Verification sent to the wrong target | Nothing of the refused call was recorded: send synchronous verify to a `direct` or `combined` server and queued work (enqueue, webhooks, deferred evidence, approvals, cancellation) to a `worker` or `combined` server; `details.target` names this server's target. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_422_INPUT_INCOMPATIBLE` | 422 | Verification input incompatible | Supply every feature the Verifier scores, with the value type its baseline or profile expects. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_422_INPUT_UNSUPPORTED` | 422 | Verification input unsupported | Execute and enqueue run request-scoped Verifiers; a Verifier that judges a scheduled window runs only on its binding schedule. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_422_TOOL_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` | 422 | Verification tool budget exceeded | Make fewer tool calls per Agent step or check, for example by reducing evidence inside one code.run program, or raise WYRD_VERIFICATION_AGENT_TOOL_MAX_CALLS on the server. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_429_STAGING_FULL` | 429 | Verification staging is full | Nothing of the refused call was staged: retry the identical call after `details.retry_after_seconds`, or lower the request rate. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_502_DEPENDENCY_FAILED` | 502 | Verification dependency failed | The agent check's provider failed after its own retries; retry the request deliberately once the provider recovers. |
| `WYRD_VERIFICATION_504_EXECUTION_TIMED_OUT` | 504 | Verification execution timed out | Reduce the supplied input or the Verifier's judge work so one execution completes within 60 seconds. |

# HTTP API

Page: /wyrd/api/openapi/

> Where a Wyrd server serves its OpenAPI document and how to use it.

Every Wyrd server serves its own OpenAPI 3.1 document at `GET /openapi.json`, without authentication. It is built from the routes that server mounts, so it always matches the version you are calling.

```bash
curl -s $WYRD_SERVER_URL/openapi.json > openapi.json
```

Load the file or the URL into any OpenAPI tool, such as Swagger UI, Redoc, Postman, or a client generator.

Each operation declares its authentication, request and response bodies, and the Wyrd error codes it can return. Errors use `application/problem+json`; see [Error codes](/wyrd/api/errors/).

The Rust, Python, and TypeScript SDKs call this same API, so you only need it for another language or for raw HTTP.
